title: Targeted release canvas and UX notes
content:
Purpose
-----
Notes + rough wireframes for a "targeted release canvas" inside Console v2: an authoring + visualizer for canary/A-B/step rollouts with explicit fallback policies. This doc is an operational working draft: UX patterns, copy ideas, edge cases, and a prioritized backlog for engineering/product.

Context and goals
- Make it fast to create a safe rollout: route X% of traffic to variant, restrict by org/route, set automatic fallback on error rate/latency/regression.
- Avoid surprising defaults: users should be able to start small, watch key signals, and promote/abort with one click.
- Surface guardrails (quota, cost, region) and what will change under Dedicated/Private deployments.

Primary personas
- Product eng (owns feature, wants low-friction rollout)
- Platform/ML infra (needs observability, rollback triggers)
- Customer success (wants precise targeting to onboard customers)

High-level flow (authoring + live canvas)
1) Create rollout (wizard or quick-action from Model/Route page)
   - Step 1: Name, description, owner, linked PR/issue (free text)
   - Step 2: Variant selection: choose model version(s) + model flavor (quantized, fp16)
   - Step 3: Traffic slices: percentages, audience filters (org id, route path, header, geo), schedule window
   - Step 4: Safety settings: duration of canary, thresholds for auto-fallback (5xx rate, mean latency, quality regression), fallback target (previous model / safe small model), notification channels
   - Step 5: Review and start (two-column diff-style review; show expected cost delta + estimated throughput)

2) Canvas view (visualizer after start)
   - Top bar: rollout name, status pill (staged / live / paused / aborted), last modification timestamp, quick actions (pause, promote, abort)
   - Main timeline: x-axis time; stacked bands represent traffic slices; succeed/fail markers; annotations auto-populated from alerts and manual notes
   - Left rail: live metrics (error rate, p50/p95 latency, tokens per request, cost burn rate, embedding similarity drift), plus a tiny sparklines list for each metric per variant
   - Right rail: audience breakdown (top orgs in slice), current routes affected, recent errors and sample traces, recent responses sample (for quality inspection), and short microcopy explaining fallback policy in effect

Wireframe components (text sketches)
- 'Traffic slice editor' card: small slider + numeric input; add filter pills ("org:acme", "path:/api/chat"); preview shows estimated RPS and token spend for that slice
- 'Safety policy editor' modal: threshold rows (metric, operator, value, evaluation window, action). Example row: [5xx_rate] [>] [0.8%] [5m] -> [auto-fallback to previous]
- 'Compare responses' view: side-by-side responses from baseline vs variant for a sample prompt set (selectable). Ability to flag samples and tie to eval tickets
- 'Promote' confirmation: small risk summary (percentage of traffic to be moved, expected latency delta, cost delta), require a short justification if promoting >50%

Microcopy & labels (quick suggestions)
- Status pills: "Staged — collecting signals", "Live — % traffic", "Paused — awaiting action", "Aborted — rolled back to baseline"
- Safety toggle tooltip: "Auto-fallback will automatically route traffic back to the chosen fallback when a threshold is breached. Recommended for production-sensitive routes."
- When adding audience filter: "Add a filter to limit this slice. e.g. org_id:1234, header:X-CLI"

Telemetry and signals to surface (minimum viable set)
- 5xx rate (per-route and global), p50/p95 latency, average tokens/request, cost/day, model-quality drift metric (use eval set mismatch score), top error classes, recent sample responses
- Recommended default thresholds: 5xx > 1% over 10m => warn; 5xx > 2% over 5m => auto-fallback (configurable)

Fallback policy examples (textual templates to seed UX)
- Conservative default (recommended): fallback if 5xx > 2% in 5m OR p95 latency > 2x baseline in 5m OR quality-drift > 0.15
- Aggressive performance-first: fallback only on 5xx > 5% or p95 > 3x baseline, used for non-critical experimental routes
- Manual-only: never auto-fallback; only send alerts (for research experiments)

Acceptance criteria for feature MVP
- Authoring: user can create a rollout with at least one traffic slice and one safety policy in <3 minutes
- Canvas: timeline updates in near real-time (<=15s delay) and shows metrics for each variant
- Fallback: when a configured threshold trips, router switches to fallback within the configured evaluation window and a clear audit entry exists
- Audit: each action (create, pause, promote, abort, auto-fallback) emits an entry with actor, timestamp, and reason visible on the canvas

Edge cases and unanswered UX decisions
- Overlapping slices: If two slices target overlapping audiences (e.g., org filters + route filters), which wins? Proposal: last-applied wins with a visual overlap indicator on canvas. Need to surface conflict resolution in review step.
- Multiple simultaneous fallbacks: if variant A falls back to baseline and variant B also fails, ensure routing evaluation is deterministic. Sketch: fallback table where chains are resolved topologically and circular fallback is rejected at authoring.
- Interactions with Dedicated/Private: privacy restrictions might hide sample responses. Canvas should gracefully degrade: show only aggregate metrics and "sample responses redacted" microcopy.

Backlog (prioritized, rough)
- P0: Traffic slice editor UI + basic authoring flow + persistence (RND-1421)
- P0: Auto-fallback engine integration + audit events
- P1: Canvas timeline and live-sparkline tiles
- P1: Side-by-side response diff and eval-set integration (link to Optimize)
- P2: Audience preview (list top 10 orgs in slice) + conflict visualization
- P2: Promote guardrail that requires justification for large changes
- P3: Pre-built policy templates and copywriting pass

Mock interaction notes (keyboard / accessibility)
- All controls should be keyboard-focusable; sliders must accept numeric input; filters should be removable by Backspace when focused
- Color: don't rely on red/green alone for state. Use icons + text (e.g., exclamation triangle + "aborted")

Open research questions
- What quality-drift metric will be available from Optimize/Applied-ML? Hook needed for the "quality drift" threshold row.
- Can Dedicated customers opt out of sample-response capture? How should canvas UI indicate the opt-out?

Next steps and owners
- UX: create clickable prototype for quick 3-step authoring (Natalie) — due 2025-11-25
- Eng: spike integration for auto-fallback runtime and audit logs (Ethan) — spike complete 2025-12-05
- Applied ML: propose a minimal quality-drift signal and API contract (Maya) — proposal 2025-11-30

Notes to self / meeting fragments
- "We should default to past-version as fallback when available; otherwise a small safe model. But need to show cost tradeoff when fallback is more expensive."
- "Think about an 'emergency abort' keyboard shortcut for SRE during incidents."
- Pending: decide retention period for rollout audit entries (30d vs 90d).
